info.description:
# Introduction

GlobalStack API for cross-border payments powered by stablecoin rails.

Getting started: authenticate with a Bearer token, make your first call to
`GET /v1/currencies`, and explore.

**Key operations:**

- **Virtual account** — a fiat wallet plus a bank credential: a named local bank
  account that credits the wallet. See the
  [virtual accounts guide](https://docs.globalstack.io/guides/virtual-accounts).
- **Onramp** — convert external fiat into crypto credited to a wallet.
- **Offramp** — convert crypto from a wallet into fiat delivered to a beneficiary.
- **Conversion** — move value between two wallets belonging to the same customer.
- **Transfer** — pay out from a wallet to a beneficiary in the same currency: a
  bank account, mobile money wallet or PayShap proxy for fiat, or an on-chain
  address for crypto.
- **Deposit** — receive funds into a wallet: a bank transfer into a credential,
  or crypto sent to a deposit address.

See the sections below for authentication, response shape, idempotency,
references, metadata, and webhooks.

## Authentication

All API requests require a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer gsa_sk_live_your_api_key
```

API keys use the `gsa_sk_live_` prefix.

API keys are scoped to a single merchant account. All resources created with
a key belong to that merchant. Keep your keys secret — do not expose them in
client-side code or public repositories.

To rotate a key, generate a new one from your dashboard and update your
integration before revoking the old key.

## API Response Shape

Every response — success or failure — follows the same envelope:

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Onramp created successfully",
  "code": "ok",
  "data": { },
  "meta": {
    "request_id": "req_01ABC...",
    "timestamp": "2026-04-22T02:00:00Z",
    "version": "1"
  }
}
```

**Fields:**

- `status` (boolean) — whether the HTTP call succeeded. This is not the
  business status of the underlying resource.
- `message` (string) — human-readable explanation for developers and logs.
  Do not show to end users.
- `code` (string) — stable machine-readable result. `ok` on success, or an
  error code like `bad_request`.
- `data` — the resource payload on success (object, array, or scalar). `null`
  on failure.
- `meta` — request-scoped metadata, always present. Includes `request_id`
  (quote this in support tickets), `timestamp`, and `version`. On list
  endpoints, also includes `page`, `per_page`, `total`, `has_more`. On
  validation errors, includes `errors` array and `next_steps`.

Error responses include `next_steps` in `meta` with an `action` string and a
`docs_url` link:

```json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Your request has validation errors.",
  "code": "bad_request",
  "data": null,
  "meta": {
    "request_id": "req_01ABC...",
    "timestamp": "2026-04-22T02:00:00Z",
    "version": "1",
    "errors": [
      { "field": "amount", "code": "required", "message": "Amount is required." }
    ],
    "next_steps": {
      "action": "Review the request and retry with corrected parameters.",
      "docs_url": "https://docs.globalstack.io/errors#bad_request"
    }
  }
}
```

## Idempotency

Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header on any create endpoint to make the request
safely retryable:

```
Idempotency-Key: your-unique-key-here
```

**Rules:**

- Same key + same body = returns the original response (no side effects).
- Same key + different body = returns `idempotency_conflict` (409).
- Keys are scoped to your merchant account.
- Keys expire after 24 hours.

Use idempotency keys for any operation that creates a resource or moves
money. This protects against network retries, duplicate webhooks, and
client-side retry loops.

## Rate Limits

Requests over the rate limit are rejected with HTTP `429` and the error code
`rate_limited`:

```json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Too many requests. Slow down and retry shortly.",
  "code": "rate_limited"
}
```

**Money-movement writes** (creating transfers, offramps, conversions, or
wallet operations) are limited **per merchant account** — the budget is
shared across all of your API keys and dashboard sessions. Reads are not
limited.

On a `429`, back off and retry with jitter; for money movement, reuse the
same `Idempotency-Key` so the retry stays safe.

## Reference

Every money movement operation (onramp, offramp, conversion, transfer)
carries a `reference` field — a merchant-supplied identifier that is unique
per merchant account. It is required on offramps, conversions and transfers.
On onramps it is optional, and the API generates one (prefixed `ref_`) when you
omit it.

```json
{
  "reference": "INV-2026-001",
  "wallet_id": "wal_..."
}
```

References are unique per merchant and never expire. Reusing one is rejected
with `409 duplicate_resource` — it does **not** return the existing operation.
To retry a request safely, resend it with the same `Idempotency-Key` instead.

Use `reference` to correlate GlobalStack operations with your own system
records (invoices, orders, payouts).

## Metadata

Most create endpoints accept an optional `metadata` object — a flat set of
string key/value pairs stored on the resource:

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "order_id": "ord_12345",
    "customer_email": "alice@example.com"
  }
}
```

Metadata is returned on every GET response and in webhook payloads. It is
not used by GlobalStack for processing — it exists for your own
record-keeping.

Resources that accept metadata: customers, wallets, senders, beneficiaries,
wallet credentials, deposit addresses, onramps, offramps, conversions, and
transfers.

## Webhook Signatures

Every webhook delivery is signed so you can verify it came from GlobalStack and
was not tampered with in transit. Signatures follow the
[Svix](https://docs.svix.com/receiving/verifying-payloads/how) standard, so you
can verify them with any Svix library — or manually with the construction below.

Each delivery carries three headers:

```
svix-id: msg_2gT8sV...          # unique message id (the body's event_id, prefixed msg_)
svix-timestamp: 1718960400      # unix seconds when the delivery was signed
svix-signature: v1,g0hM9SsE...  # space-separated list of v1,<base64-signature>
```

Your signing secret (prefixed `whsec_`) is returned in plaintext **exactly
once** — when you create a webhook endpoint or rotate its secret. Store it
securely; you cannot retrieve it again.

**Verify with a Svix library (recommended):**

```python
from svix.webhooks import Webhook

wh = Webhook(signing_secret)                            # the whsec_... value
payload = wh.verify(raw_request_body, request_headers)  # raises on a bad signature
```

**Verify manually:**

1. Build the signed content by joining the id, timestamp, and the **raw**
   request body with dots:

   ```
   signed_content = svix_id + "." + svix_timestamp + "." + raw_body
   ```

2. Take your signing secret, drop the `whsec_` prefix, and base64-decode the
   remainder — those bytes are your HMAC key.

3. Compute `base64(HMAC-SHA256(key, signed_content))`.

4. The `svix-signature` header is a space-separated list of `v1,<signature>`
   entries (an endpoint can have more than one valid secret during a rotation).
   Compare your computed value against each entry's signature — the part after
   `v1,` — using a constant-time comparison, and accept if any matches.

5. Reject deliveries whose `svix-timestamp` differs from your current time by
   more than a few minutes, to guard against replay.

The body's `event_id` equals the `svix-id` without its `msg_` prefix, so you can
use either to deduplicate redelivered events.

## Request IDs

Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header (also surfaced in
`meta.request_id`). Include the value when reporting issues — it scopes
backend logs to your specific request.

You may also send your own `X-Request-Id` header. Values matching
`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$` are honored verbatim; anything else is replaced with
a generated id.

## Versioning

Public endpoints are versioned under `/v1/`. Breaking changes ship under a new
major version; additive changes (new fields, new endpoints) ship under the
existing version.

Create a wallet: a balance in one currency, owned by a customer.

A wallet has no account details on its own. To receive bank transfers into it, add a
[credential](https://docs.globalstack.io/guides/virtual-accounts) with
`POST /v1/wallets/{id}/credentials`. You can still onramp into a wallet that has no credentials.

### Body

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currency` | Yes | Currency code, e.g. `USDC`, `NGN`. Must support deposits (`can_deposit`). |
| `customer_id` | No | The owner (`cust_…`). Omit it to create the wallet for your own merchant account. |
| `country_code` | No | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Required only when the currency code exists in more than one country, e.g. `XOF`. Ignored for crypto. |
| `type` | No | `custodial` (default) or `forwarding`. See below. |
| `destination_address` | No | Required for a `forwarding` wallet, and rejected otherwise. Where a forwarding wallet sends funds. Max 128 chars, valid for `destination_chain`. |
| `destination_chain` | No | Required for a `forwarding` wallet, and rejected otherwise. `solana`, `base` or `ethereum`, and supported by `currency`. |
| `label` | No | Max 255 chars. Use it to tell wallets apart. |
| `metadata` | No | `Record<string, string>`. |

- **Verified customers only for fiat.** A fiat wallet for a customer whose `kyc_status` isn't
  `approved` returns `409 invalid_status`. See
  [Verify customers](https://docs.globalstack.io/guides/verify-customers).
- **One wallet per fiat currency** per customer. A customer can hold several wallets in the same
  crypto currency.
- **Pinned country.** `country_code` is stored on the wallet and used by quotes and deposit
  addresses, so the wallet can serve payers outside the customer's KYC country.

| `type` | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `custodial` | Holds a balance. Deposits credit it, and you convert, offramp and transfer out of it. |
| `forwarding` | Holds nothing. Every inflow goes straight to `destination_address`. Crypto only. It can't be the source of a transfer, offramp or conversion, and its destination can't be changed later. |

`tier`). For the full customer, call `GET /v1/customers/{customerId}`.

### Errors

| Status | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_input` | The currency isn't supported, isn't supported in `country_code`, or exists in several countries and `country_code` is missing. Also when a forwarding wallet's fields are invalid, or are sent for a custodial wallet. |
| 409 | `invalid_status` | Fiat currency, and the customer's KYC isn't approved. |
| 409 | `duplicate_resource` | The customer already has a wallet in this fiat currency. |

### Examples

```
POST /v1/wallets
{ "currency": "NGN", "customer_id": "cust_01HXYZ…", "label": "Ada — NGN" }
```

```
POST /v1/wallets
{
  "currency": "USDC",
  "type": "forwarding",
  "destination_address": "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
  "destination_chain": "base"
}
```

post.description:
Pay out from a wallet to a beneficiary in the **same currency**. The beneficiary decides where the
money goes: a fiat beneficiary pays a bank account, mobile money wallet or PayShap proxy, and a
crypto beneficiary pays an on-chain address.

The transfer starts as `processing` and then becomes `success` or `failed`. Follow it with the
`transfer.*` webhooks.

### Body

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wallet_id` | Yes | The wallet to pay from (`wal_…`). |
| `beneficiary_id` | Yes | Who to pay (`ben_…`). Must be in the wallet's currency. |
| `amount` | Yes | Decimal string, within the network's outbound limits. |
| `reference` | Yes | Your id, unique per integration and never reusable. A reused one returns `409 duplicate_resource`. |
| `source_currency`, `destination_currency` | No | If sent, they must match the wallet and beneficiary currencies. |
| `metadata` | No | `Record<string, string>`. |

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header so retries are safe.

### Fiat transfers

| Currency | Destination | Beneficiary needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NGN | Bank | 10-digit NUBAN + bank `provider_id` |
| ZAR | Bank | Account number + the bank's `provider_id` + `account_name` |
| ZAR | PayShap | Mobile number (E.164) or ShapName |
| GHS | Bank | Account number + bank `provider_id` |
| GHS | Mobile money | Mobile number + operator `provider_id` |

**Fees are added on top.** The beneficiary receives `amount` in full, and your wallet is debited
`amount + fee`. The wallet must hold both, or the request fails with
`422 ledger_insufficient_funds`. The response shows the charge as `fee: { amount, currency }`.

**To know the fee in advance**, read your route's schedule from
`fees.payment_methods[].transfer` on `GET /v1/currencies`:

1. Take the tiers whose `[transaction_value_min, transaction_value_max]` range contains your
   amount. Both ends are inclusive.
2. Sort them by `weight`, lowest first.
3. For each tier, deduct `max(min_fee, min(raw, max_fee))` from a running net. `raw` is
   `fee_value` for a `flat` tier, or `net × fee_value / 100` for a `percentage` tier.
4. The fee is the sum of the deductions, rounded down to 2 decimal places.

A route with no published schedule is refused with `400 invalid_input` before the transfer is
created, so your `reference` stays unused.

### Crypto transfers

- No fee: `fee` is `null`.
- USDC settles in whole cents, so `amount` can have at most **2 decimal places**, ignoring trailing zeros.
  `2.980000` is fine, but `2.980228` returns `400 invalid_amount_precision`.

### Errors

| Status | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_input` | Currencies don't match, the beneficiary is missing details its route needs, or the route has no fee schedule. |
| 400 | `invalid_amount_precision` | USDC amount with more than 2 decimal places. |
| 409 | `duplicate_resource` | `reference` already used. |
| 422 | `ledger_insufficient_funds` | The balance doesn't cover `amount` (+ `fee` for fiat). |

### Example

```
POST /v1/transfers
Idempotency-Key: payout-inv-2026-001
{
  "wallet_id": "wal_01HXYZ…",
  "beneficiary_id": "ben_01KPBAP…",
  "amount": "250.00",
  "reference": "payout-inv-2026-001"
}
```

get.description:
List onramps, newest first. Results are scoped to
the authenticated integration.

All filters are optional. With no filters every onramp for the integration is
returned (paginated).

### Filter behavior

- `customer_id` — restricts to onramps for a single customer. Must be a valid
  `cust_…` id. An unknown id returns an empty page (`200`,
  `data: []`), not `404`.
- `status` — restricts to a single lifecycle status. One of `created`,
  `awaiting_deposit`, `processing`, `temporary_failure`, `success`, `failed`,
  `returned`.
- `created_after` / `created_before` — either a `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date (UTC,
  inclusive: `created_after` matches at or after `00:00:00`, `created_before` at
  or before `23:59:59.999`) or a full ISO 8601 UTC timestamp ending in `Z`
  (e.g. `2026-04-16T16:16:03Z`), used as the exact instant.

### Pagination

- `page` — 1-indexed page number. Defaults to `1`. Must be between `1` and `1,000,000`.
- `per_page` — page size. Defaults to `50`. Must be between `1` and `200`.

The response carries pagination metadata under `meta`:

```json
"meta": {
  "request_id": "req_...",
  "timestamp": "...",
  "version": "1",
  "page": 1,
  "per_page": 50,
  "total": 137,
  "has_more": true
}
```

`has_more` is `true` when at least one more page is available.

### Ordering

Results are sorted by `created_at DESC, id DESC` (newest first, deterministic on
ties).

### Example

```
GET /v1/onramps?status=awaiting_deposit&customer_id=cust_seed_alice&page=1&per_page=50
```

post.description:
Register an HTTPS endpoint to receive webhook events for your integration.

Subscribe to one or more **event categories** — coarse families of events rather than
individual topics. The available categories are: `onramp`, `offramp`, `conversion`,
`transfer`, `deposit`, `kyc`.

Every event in a subscribed category is delivered. For the events each category contains,
when each one fires, and the payload it carries, see
[Webhook events](https://docs.globalstack.io/webhooks/events).

The response includes a **`signing_secret`** (prefixed `whsec_`) returned **in plaintext
exactly once** — on create and on rotate-secret only. Store it securely; you cannot retrieve
it again. Use it to verify the signature on every delivered event.

New endpoints are created **inactive** (`active: false`). Activate the endpoint with a
`PATCH` once you have stored the signing secret and are ready to receive deliveries.

### Body

- `url` — required. Must be a valid **HTTPS** URL.
- `event_categories` — required. Non-empty array of event categories (see above). Unknown
  values are rejected with `400`.

### Example

```
POST /v1/notifications/webhooks
{
  "url": "https://merchant.example.com/webhooks",
  "event_categories": ["onramp", "conversion"]
}
```

Update a webhook endpoint. This is a partial update — supply only the fields you want to
change. At least one field is required.

change which `event_categories` it is subscribed to. Updating `event_categories` **replaces**

- `url` — a valid **HTTPS** URL.
- `event_categories` — non-empty array of event categories; replaces the current set.

}

post.description:
Creates a new customer scoped to the calling merchant's integration.

### Body

- `type` — required. One of `individual`, `business`.
- `name` — required. Full name of the customer. Max 255 chars.
- `email` — required. Valid email. Max 255 chars. Per-integration uniqueness
  is enforced case-insensitively.
- `country_code` — required. ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 (e.g. `NG`, `KE`). Countries on the
  compliance prohibited list are rejected with `400 prohibited_country`.
- `metadata` — optional. Free-form `Record<string, string>`.
- `merchant_reference` — optional. Max 128 chars. Auto-generated as
  `ref_<ULID>` when omitted. Per-integration unique.
- `profile` — optional object carrying the identity fields required to convert
  (onramp/offramp). When supplied it must be complete for the customer `type`:
  - `individual` requires `phone`, `address`, `date_of_birth`, `id_number`, `id_type`.
  - `business` requires `phone`, `business_licence`.

  Fields: `phone`, `address`, `id_number`, `id_type`, `business_licence` are strings;
  `date_of_birth` must be `mm/dd/yyyy`. A supplied-but-incomplete `profile` for the
  `type` returns `400 invalid_input`.

### Example

```

{
  "type": "individual",
  "name": "Alice Johnson",
  "email": "alice@example.com",
  "country_code": "NG",
  "profile": {
    "phone": "+2348012345678",
    "address": "1 Marina Rd, Lagos",
    "date_of_birth": "01/15/1990",
    "id_number": "A12345678",
    "id_type": "passport"

unchanged.

| --- | --- |
| `name` | Max 255 chars. Individuals still need a first and last name. |

`400 bad_request`.

```

{ "profile": { "phone": "+233201234567" } }

post.description:
Creates a hosted verification session for a customer scoped to the calling
integration. The returned `hosted_url` is the hosted verification link that
the merchant must surface to their customer to complete verification.

### Path

- `customer_id` — required. The `cust_…` external id of an existing,
  non-default customer that belongs to the calling integration.

### Body

- `tier` — optional. One of `tier_1`, `tier_2`. Defaults to the next tier
  above the customer's current tier (`tier_0` → `tier_1`; `tier_1` →
  `tier_2`). `tier_0` is never a valid requested tier.
- `redirect_url` — optional. HTTPS URL the merchant wants the customer
  redirected to after the verification flow completes. Stored verbatim and
  echoed back on the response.

### Replay & link refresh

If a `pending` session already exists for the same `(customer_id,
tier_requested)` and its `hosted_url_expires_at` is in the future, this
endpoint returns that existing session unchanged — no second upstream call.
Clients can safely retry POSTs without an Idempotency-Key header.

If that `pending` session exists but its `hosted_url` has **expired**, this
endpoint mints a fresh hosted link and refreshes the same session in place,

get.description:
List the currencies GlobalStack supports, with what each can do, its networks and limits, and its fees.

Each row is one currency in one country. For example, every country that uses `XOF` has its own
row. For countries, start with `GET /v1/countries`. For the banks and mobile money operators you
need as a beneficiary `provider_id`, use `GET /v1/countries/{country_code}/providers`.

### What each row tells you

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `can_onramp`, `can_offramp`, `can_deposit`, `can_convert`, `can_transfer` | What the currency supports. For fiat, `can_onramp` means it can be paid in for an onramp, and `can_offramp` means it can be paid out by an offramp. |
| `networks` | Settlement networks (`bank`, `mobile_money`, chains), each with inbound and outbound min/max amounts. |
| `fees` | Fee schedules per network, under `fees.payment_methods`. Split into `onramp`, `offramp` and `transfer` where supported. `null` for crypto, or when fee data is unavailable. |
| `requires_access`, `has_access` | Whether the currency must be enabled for your account, and whether it is. See [Currency access](https://docs.globalstack.io/essentials/currency-access). |
| `customer_restrictions` | Only with `customer_id`. See below. |

### For a specific customer

By default the flags describe the platform, so every caller sees the same values. Add
`customer_id` to ask what **that customer** can do right now. Today, fiat `can_deposit` reads
`false` until the customer's KYC is approved, and the row then carries a `customer_restrictions`
entry explaining why:

```json
"customer_restrictions": [
  { "capability": "deposit", "reason": "customer_kyc_not_approved",
    "next_steps": { "action": "…", "docs_url": "…" } }
]
```

Restrictions appear only for capabilities the platform supports but the customer can't use yet.
Filters like `can_deposit=true` apply to the customer's view too. See
[Customer restrictions](https://docs.globalstack.io/reference/customer-restrictions).

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `code` | Currency code. `XOF` returns every WAEMU country. |
| `type` | `fiat` or `crypto`. |
| `country_code` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. |
| `customer_id` | Switch to that customer's view (`cust_…`). |
| `can_onramp`, `can_offramp`, `can_transfer`, `can_deposit`, `can_convert` | `true` or `false`. |

The list isn't paginated: every matching currency comes back in one response.

### Errors

| Status | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_input` | `customer_id` is malformed. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `customer_id` doesn't exist, or belongs to another integration. |

### Example

```
GET /v1/currencies?type=fiat&can_offramp=true
```

post.description:
Add a way to pay into a wallet. A **bank** credential gives you a named local bank account, a
[virtual account](https://docs.globalstack.io/guides/virtual-accounts). A **crypto** credential
gives you an on-chain address.

### Body

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `network` | Yes | `bank` for fiat (the only fiat network today, so `mobile_money` is rejected). For crypto: `solana`, `base` or `ethereum`. |
| `currency` | No | Omit it to match the wallet. Send a different currency for an auto-converting credential (below). |
| `country_code` | No | Needed when `currency` exists in several countries, e.g. `XOF`. For a same-currency credential it must match the wallet's country. |
| `type` | No | `fiat` or `crypto`. Inferred from the currency. If sent, it must match. |
| `label` | No | Max 128 chars. |
| `metadata` | No | `Record<string, string>`. |
| `merchantReference` | No | Your id. Generated if omitted. |

### Bank credentials (virtual accounts)

- **The customer must be verified.** If the wallet's owner hasn't passed KYC, you get
  `409 invalid_status`.
- **Some currencies need extra customer details.** GHS needs a phone number. NGN needs a phone
  number and, for individuals, a date of birth and address. Put them on the customer's `profile`
  before you create the credential. A missing GHS phone, or a missing NGN date of birth or address,
  is rejected with `400 invalid_input` naming the field.
- **It may start `pending`.** Fetch the credential until `status` is `active`. `details` then
  holds `accountName`, `accountNumber`, `bankName`, `bankCode` and `currency`.
- **Deposit reference.** Some ZAR accounts also return `details.reference`. The payer must quote it,
  or the deposit can't be matched automatically. If it's absent, no reference is needed.

### Auto-converting credentials

Send a `currency` different from the wallet's, and every deposit converts into the wallet's
currency at the rate at deposit time. Only fiat ↔ crypto pairs are allowed.

| Credential | Wallet | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fiat (e.g. `NGN`, network `bank`) | Crypto (e.g. `USDC`) | **Auto-onramp.** The payer sends fiat, and the wallet is credited in crypto. Both currencies need `can_onramp`. |
| Crypto (e.g. `USDC`, network `base`) | Fiat (e.g. `NGN`) | **Auto-offramp.** The payer sends crypto, and the wallet is credited in fiat. Both need `can_offramp`. |

`network` is checked against the credential's own currency. See
[Auto-conversion](https://docs.globalstack.io/guides/auto-conversion).

### Errors

| Status | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_input` | Unsupported network, a fiat network other than `bank`, a mismatched `type` or `country_code`, an unsupported currency pair, or missing customer details. |
| 409 | `invalid_status` | Fiat credential, and the customer's KYC isn't approved. |

### Example

```
POST /v1/wallets/wal_01HXYZ…/credentials
{ "network": "bank", "label": "Ama — collections" }
```

post.description:
Save a payout destination: a bank account, mobile money wallet or PayShap proxy (`fiat`), or an
on-chain address (`crypto`). You then pay it with a transfer or an offramp.

Send every field at the top level. On read, account details are nested under `details`, and
`provider_id` is expanded to `provider`. For a walkthrough, see
[Beneficiaries](https://docs.globalstack.io/guides/beneficiaries).

### Body: every beneficiary

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | Yes | `fiat` or `crypto`. |
| `name` | Yes | Max 255 chars. |
| `label` | Yes | A short tag for your UI. Max 128 chars. |
| `currency` | Yes | e.g. `NGN`, `USDC`. |
| `customer_id` | No | Owner (`cust_…`). Omit it for your own merchant account. |
| `merchant_reference` | No | Your id, unique per integration. Max 128 chars. Generated as `ref_…` if omitted. |
| `metadata` | No | `Record<string, string>`. |

### Body: fiat

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `country_code` | Yes | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. `NG`. |
| `network` | Yes | `bank` or `mobile_money`: what the destination is. |
| `rail` | No | How money reaches it. Only `payshap`, which is valid only for `ZAR` bank in `ZA`. Omit it for the default. |
| `account_number` | Yes | A bank account number, a mobile number for `mobile_money`, or a PayShap proxy (an E.164 mobile number, or a ShapName like `acme@nedbank`, exactly as given). |
| `provider_id` | Yes | The bank or operator (`prov_…`), from `GET /v1/countries/{code}/providers`. Not needed for PayShap: ignored if sent, though still format-checked. |
| `account_name` | No | Optional where we look the name up: `NGN` and `GHS` bank accounts, and PayShap. Your value is then replaced by the looked-up name. Required everywhere else, including mobile money. |

### Body: crypto

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `network` | Yes | `solana`, `base` or `ethereum`. |
| `address` | Yes | Max 128 chars. |

### Errors

| Status | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_input` | The currency, network or rail isn't supported for this country, or a required field for the destination is missing. |
| 400 | `account_resolution_failed` | The bank couldn't confirm the account. Check `account_number` and `provider_id`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `customer_id` doesn't exist in your integration. |
| 409 | `duplicate_resource` | `merchant_reference` is already used. |

### Examples

```
POST /v1/beneficiaries
{
  "type": "fiat", "currency": "NGN", "country_code": "NG", "network": "bank",
  "provider_id": "prov_01KPBAP7WTDKQKW5B3R31VPNX4", "account_number": "0039415616",
  "name": "Alice Bank Beneficiary", "label": "Alice's salary account"
}
```

```
POST /v1/beneficiaries
{
  "type": "crypto", "currency": "USDC", "network": "solana", "address": "9wFFa…",
  "name": "Alice Wallet", "label": "Personal cold wallet"
}
```

get.description:
List beneficiaries for your merchant account.

All filters are optional. When no filters are supplied every merchant's beneficiary is returned (paginated).

### Filter behavior

- `customer_id` — restricts to beneficiaries owned by the named GlobalStack
  customer (`cust_<ULID>`). Returns 404 if the customer is unknown.
- `type` — restricts to beneficiaries of the given type. One of `fiat`, `crypto`.
- `currency` — restricts to beneficiaries with the given uppercase currency
  code (2-8 alphanumerics). Matched literally against stored values.

### Pagination

- `page` — 1-indexed page number. Defaults to `1`. Must be between `1` and `1,000,000`.
- `per_page` — page size. Defaults to `50`. Must be between `1` and `200`.

The response carries pagination metadata under `meta`:

```json
"meta": {
  "request_id": "req_...",
  "timestamp": "...",
  "version": "1",
  "page": 1,
  "per_page": 50,
  "total": 12,
  "has_more": false
}
```

`has_more` is `true` when at least one more page is available.

### Ordering

Results are sorted by `created_at DESC, id DESC` (newest first, deterministic on ties).

### Example

```
GET /v1/beneficiaries?customer_id=cust_01KPBAP7WTDKQKW5B3R31VPNX4&type=fiat&currency=NGN&page=1&per_page=25
```

patch.description:
Update a beneficiary. Send only the fields you're changing. Returns the beneficiary, in the
same shape as create.

### What you can change

| Can change | Can't change |
| --- | --- |
| `name`, `label`, `metadata`, `merchant_reference` | `type`, `customer_id`, `currency`, `country_code`. Create a new beneficiary instead. |
| Fiat: `network`, `rail`, `account_number`, `account_name`, `provider_id` | |
| Crypto: `network`, `address` | |

### Rules

- **`metadata`** replaces the whole map, with no merge.
- **`merchant_reference`** can be replaced, but not cleared with `null`.
- **Changing a fiat `network`** needs a new `provider_id` too, except for PayShap.
- **`rail`**: omit it to keep the current rail, send `null` to go back to the default, or send a
  value to set it.
- **Changing `rail`** needs a new `account_number` too, because the rail decides what that number
  means. Leaving PayShap also needs a `provider_id`.
- **`provider_id`** on its own is ignored for PayShap.
- The result must pass the same checks as create: a supported currency, network and rail for the
  country, and an `account_name` for mobile money.
- **Archived** beneficiaries can't be updated.

### Errors

| Status | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `bad_request` | Field validation failed, an immutable field was sent, or `merchant_reference` is `null`. |
| 400 | `invalid_input` | A cross-field rule is broken, e.g. a `network` change without `provider_id`, or the result fails a currency or network check. |
| 404 | `not_found` | No beneficiary with this id in your integration. |
| 409 | `invalid_status` | The beneficiary is archived. |
| 409 | `duplicate_resource` | `merchant_reference` is used by another beneficiary. |
| 500 | `external_service_unavailable` | The provider lookup failed. Retry. |

### Examples

```
PATCH /v1/beneficiaries/ben_01KPBAP7WTDKQKW5B3R31VPNX4
{ "account_number": "0099887766" }
```

Switch from bank to mobile money:

```
PATCH /v1/beneficiaries/ben_01KPBAP7WTDKQKW5B3R31VPNX4
{
  "network": "mobile_money",
  "provider_id": "prov_01KPBBNEWPR0V1DERZZZZZZZ4M",
  "account_number": "+2348012345678",
  "account_name": "Alice Johnson"
}
```

delete.description:
Deactivates a beneficiary by changing its `status` to `archived`. The
beneficiary record is preserved — list and get continue to return it.

The path id is the GlobalStack external identifier (`ben_…`).

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Beneficiary has been successfully deactivated",
  "code": "ok",
  "data": {
    "id": "ben_01KPBAP7WTDKQKW5B3R31VPNX4",
    "success": true
  },
  "meta": { "request_id": "req_…", "timestamp": "…", "version": "1" }
}
```

### Status preconditions

- `pending` → archived.
- `active` → archived.
- `archived` → `409 invalid_status` (not idempotent).

### Errors

- `400 invalid_input` — `beneficiary_id` does not start with `ben_`.
- `404 not_found` — id does not exist or belongs to a different
  integration.
- `409 invalid_status` — beneficiary is already archived.

### Example

```
DELETE /v1/beneficiaries/ben_01KPBAP7WTDKQKW5B3R31VPNX4
```
